chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has servants upon the earth from among the sincere ones of His servants. No gift descends from the heaven to the earth except that He turns it away from them to others, and no affliction descends except that He turns it toward them.

key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the heaven, from where decrees and provisions descend
key_terms.بَلِيَّةً: an affliction, trial, or severe test
key_terms.تُحْفَةً: a gift or present sent down as a worldly favor
key_terms.خَالِصِ: pure and sincere, free of mixed motives in devotion
key_terms.صَرَفَهَا: He turned it away or redirected it
key_terms.عِبَادِهِ: His servants, meaning those devoted to Allah

ai.seo_question: Why do Allah’s sincere servants receive more afflictions instead of worldly blessings?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a special group among Allah’s sincere servants whose share in this world is not worldly gifts, but affliction and trial. It highlights the spiritual rank of the sincere believers and shows that hardship may be a sign of divine selection rather than rejection.
